title: Agreement, prevalence and adjudication uncertainty
outcome: Calculate agreement with the correct marginals, explain prevalence effects, and distinguish reliable labels from valid labels.

exercises.title: Reconstruct the confusion table
exercises.task: Rebuild the table in case A by counting label pairs.
exercises.expected: Rows A and columns B give [[2,0],[1,1]].
exercises.answer: Two negative-negative pairs, one positive-negative pair and one positive-positive pair determine both marginals and agreement.

exercises.title: Perfect variation
exercises.answer: There is perfect observed agreement with nondegenerate marginals, so the corrected coefficient is defined and equals 1.

exercises.title: Complete disagreement
exercises.hint: Observed agreement is 0 and expected agreement is 0.5.
exercises.answer: A negative coefficient means less agreement than the marginal reference, not a negative count of labels.

exercises.title: Single-category degeneracy
exercises.hint: Its denominator is 1 minus expected agreement.
exercises.answer: Both raw and reference agreement are 1. The coefficient becomes 0/0, so preserve the degeneracy instead of replacing it with an attractive score.

exercises.title: Distinguish weighted quantities
exercises.task: Compare observed ordinal disagreement to weighted kappa.
exercises.expected: The implemented quantity lacks an expected-disagreement correction.
exercises.hint: List numerator and denominator for each definition.
exercises.answer: Observed squared-distance disagreement is useful descriptively, but weighted kappa would normalize it by expected disagreement under marginals.

exercises.title: Change the dependence unit
exercises.task: Annotate ten paraphrases from each of two families.
exercises.expected: The evaluation still has two sampled families.
exercises.hint: Count independent groups, not annotation cells.
exercises.answer: Additional paraphrases may reveal within-family variation, but family-level uncertainty cannot treat twenty rows as twenty independent sampled families.
